title: Cross-process 1v1 vs TagDuel acceptance lock race
priority: P1 — provar exclusão mútua real entre Accept 1v1 e Accept TagDuel sob concorrência entre processos: duas conexões SQLite independentes não podem adquirir simultaneamente os locks do mesmo jogador.

design.isolation: temporary SQLite file seeded by the parent process; parent connection closed before workers start
design.concurrency: two independent Node child processes, each with its own better-sqlite3 connection; both workers signal ready before the parent releases both Accept transactions
design.invariant: exactly one acceptance and exactly one invitee lock (duel_members XOR tag_members)

assertions: both invitations are pending and the invitee initially owns neither lock
exactly one process commits its acceptance
the losing transaction fails closed with a cross-mode conflict or SQLite busy error
persisted duel/lobby state agrees with the winning lock table
original host and duel-creator locks remain intact
players, player_cards, starter_grants, decks and deck_cards are byte-equivalent before and after
limitations: Process-level concurrency against temporary SQLite; no production database.
Uses the real duelStore/tagStore acceptance transactions, not a live Discord gateway.
The test proves lock exclusivity; it does not claim a friendly user-facing retry message for SQLITE_BUSY.
